summary.headline: FY26 total income rose 60% to ₹368 crores, but PAT only edged up to ₹20.5 crores as finance costs hit ₹10.5 crores and gross margin fell to ~30%.
summary.overview: Solarium Green Energy reported FY26 total income of ₹368 crores (up 60% YoY) and EBITDA of ₹35.3 crores (~9.6% margin), with PAT of ₹20.5 crores. Growth came from large ground-mounted EPC projects, which carry lower gross margins; gross margin fell to ~30% from 34.5%. Finance costs rose to ₹10.5 crores from ₹3.5 crores as the 1.2 GW module plant was financed, and receivables and inventory built up. The 1.2 GW Ahmedabad module facility began production only in mid-March 2026 and was running at ~45% utilisation at the time of the call.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹79 crores at 34.5% in FY25; gross profit +40% YoY

segments.name: C&I and ground-mounted EPC
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to ₹227 crores from ₹114 crores in FY25. Management attributes growth mainly to large EPC execution; a 50 MW AC ground-mounted project in Maharashtra was won at over ₹185 crores.

segments.name: Essential rooftop / residential
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹80 crores in FY26 (end-to-end installations); management says a ~₹10-12 crore monthly run rate excluding kits over the last 3-4 months.

segments.name: Distribution (incl. solar kits)
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹61 crores, partly reflecting reclassification of solar kit revenue into this vertical; kit sales added ~₹14 crores in FY26.

segments.name: Module manufacturing (1.2 GW, Ahmedabad)
segments.commentary: Commissioned in FY26 with production starting mid-March 2026; ~45% utilisation, with output so far used in distribution sales. External module orders on hand are ~₹35-40 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 10-12%; management confirmed exit FY27 margin of ~10-12% when asked, versus ~8-9% currently cited by an analyst.
Margins expected to be 'minimally protected' at FY26 levels, with no further fall anticipated as the business moves to a lower fixed-cost model.
Revenue expected to grow at least at the rate of the past couple of years, with growth expected to accelerate as the manufacturing facility goes live.
Manufacturing targeted at gross/overall margins above 15% on a cost-plus basis.
Finance cost to fall as a share of revenue as manufacturing assets generate returns; absolute interest cost expected to stay in a similar range or rise marginally.
No major capex planned in FY27; focus on execution and ramp-up.
Pipeline conversion of ~60% of the ~300 MW EPC pipeline expected within 2-3 months (per Ankit Garg); separately, conversion expected over 3-6 months per Himanshu Garg.
capex_capacity: 1.2 GW fully automated module plant in Ahmedabad commissioned; capable of 4,000 panels/day at up to 23.5% cell efficiency, including G12 panels up to 725 Wp.
Plant utilisation ~45%; utilisation was cut for ~10 days to assess market response to the ALMM-II circular.
Targeted in-house consumption of 50-60% of production: 40-50% via own EPC projects, plus solar kits and other EPC players' orders.
Confirmed captive module consumption of ~65 MW within EPC order book; forward pipeline of 300+ MW under discussion.
CAPEX for the module plant ~₹90 crores, plus ~₹100 crores working capital.
demand_pricing: Executed order book exceeds ₹300 crores; management says almost 100% will execute within FY27.
Ground-mounted EPC order in hand ~₹185 crores; large project receivables expected to be much shorter, with a ₹150 crore project needing under ₹30-35 crores of working capital.
Residential end-to-end monthly run rate ~₹10-12 crores; expected ₹16-18 crores including solar kits by calendar year-end.
Sarathi partner network above 450 partners across 25+ cities; company ranks second among 20,000+ vendors under PM Surya Ghar.

ALMM-II: order book largely covers projects bid before 31 August 2025 where non-domestic cells remain allowed; company says it is at an advanced stage of securing domestic cells for residential EPC and kits.
Management says cell capacity of ~30 GW is expected to be sufficient within 6-8 months; cost-plus pricing means cell price increases are passed through to customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the factory utilisation and how will output split between captive and external sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is ~45%, reduced for 10 days due to ALMM-II. Management targets 50-60% in-house consumption (EPC, solar kits, other EPC players), with the rest sold externally.

qa_highlights.question: How is client and project concentration managed in large EPC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said concentrated large sites reduce the number of decision-makers versus many distributed sites (200-250 sites executed earlier), so focus has moved to bigger ground-mounted projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins expected to be minimally protected at FY26 levels; revenue growth expected at least at past rates, accelerating with the factory. No numeric FY27 guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the debt levels, interest cost and repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹100 crores-plus of working capital overdraft, repayable on demand, plus a ~₹50 crore term loan repayable over six years. FY26 interest cost was ₹10.5 crores; management did not expect it to reach ₹30-35 crores in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the increase in other current liabilities from ₹4 crores to ₹36 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹19 crores is payable to creditors for fixed assets (capex) classified as current liabilities, ~₹2 crores is year-end employee payables, and ~₹5.5 crores is advances from customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for the manufacturing business and how does domestic cell sourcing affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets above 15% gross/overall margin on a cost-plus model and expects at least ~15% margin to hold, though market conditions may shift over 3-6 months.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from the shift to lower-margin ground-mounted EPC; FY26 gross margin ~30% vs 34.5%.
Finance cost burden: ₹100 crores-plus of repayable-on-demand working capital debt; FY26 finance cost ₹10.5 crores vs ₹3.5 crores.
Working capital intensity: trade receivables up to ₹152.6 crores from ₹90.9 crores.
ALMM-II and domestic cell availability/pricing; management noted a new MNRE circular requiring monthly price declarations.
Low factory utilisation (~45%) and reliance on captive demand; conversion of the 300 MW pipeline is uncertain (a single 100 MW award is binary).
Project concentration in a 150 MW Maharashtra project; analyst noted it is a significant portion of revenue.
Inconsistent figures on call: EBITDA margin cited as ~9.5% and ~8-9%; management's FY27 guidance of 10-12% exit margin is a key test.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on strategy and the ramp-up, but cautious and at times vague on numbers such as utilisation timing, cell sourcing and conversion rates. Management avoided a direct answer on the PAT trajectory and gave no formal numeric FY27 revenue guidance.
key_quotes: We consciously added ground mounted large EPC project as another scheme for the business.
We do not see ALM M-II as an unmanageable constraint and in fact our manufacturing scale position us reasonably well at the broader industry transition towards the greater domestic content.

In a larger ground -mounted, generally, unlike the 120, 150 days kind of cycle in government projects, in these sort of projects , we generally kind of keep getting the money during the execution itself.
